ofek-melika.why: G2P said mi-LI-ka for the bare name but me-LI-ka inside the match phrase; me-LI-ka is the reading of מליקה.

raz-shlomo.why: Colloquial Israeli stress SHLO-mo (G2P gave the formal shlo-MO).

issouf-sissokho.why: G2P was inconsistent (si-so-KO / si-su-KO); pinned to i-SUF si-SO-ko, the natural Hebrew reading of the French name.

helio-varela.why: G2P read וארלה as ve-AR-la and הליו as HAL-yo; the player is Hélio Varela: HEL-yo va-RE-la. Without a break the v slid onto the first name (STT: הליוב ארלה); the comma adds a short beat between the names (name 5/6 vs 1/6).

mohamed-ali-camara.why: G2P correct (mu-KHA-mad a-LI ka-MA-ra). Three words, so paced a little faster to stay near 1.5 s.

osher-davida.why: Bare-name G2P correct; pinned because the match-phrase G2P drifted to o-SHER.

ido-shahar.why: Colloquial Israeli stress I-do (G2P gave the formal i-DO).

ester-sokler.why: G2P said AS-ter; the Slovenian name is ES-ter SOK-ler.

noam-ben-harush.why: G2P said ha-ROSH; the surname is ha-RUSH. With a single h the voice dropped it after 'ben' in 12/12 takes (STT: בן ארוש); the doubled hh keeps it audible (12/12).

tyrese-asante.why: G2P ended Asante with -ta; tai-RIS a-SAN-te follows the Hebrew spelling טייריס אסנטה.

itay-ben-hemo.why: G2P kept (i-TAI ben khe-MO); stress of חמו is not certain, flagged for a listen.

james-tavernier.why: Bare-name G2P kept (JEIMS ta-VER-nyer). Israeli media spell him טברנייר / טאברנייר, so the final r stays (not the English TAV-er-nee-ay). Pinned because the match phrase drifted to te-VER-nyer. STT has no fixed spelling for this new name: ניאר spells the same -nier ending as דניאל (Da-ni-EL), and ו/ב are both v.

elad-madmon.why: Dropped the formal glottal stop of ע (e-LAD, as Israelis say it).

hisham-layous.why: G2P garbled both words; the name is hi-SHAM la-YUS. The opening h was lost in most name takes (STT: אישם); the doubled hh fixed it (12/12).

ilay-ben-simon.why: G2P's i-LAI is right, but the voice collapsed the -ai diphthong into 'Ili' (STT: אילי, 0/6 match takes). Splitting it as i-la-'I brings back עילאי (10/12).

kristijan-belic.why: G2P dropped the e of Belić (BLICH); kris-TYAN BE-lich.

roi-mishpati.why: G2P read משפתי as mish-fa-TIJ (an f, and a stray j); the club writes Mishpati, said mish-pa-TI as the spelling reads (12/12 STT round-trips against 9/12 for mish-PA-ti, A/B gk-ab). רועי as ro-I, like Hapoel's roei-alkukin: RO-ʔi came back as «רוי» (Roy) on 33 of 40 name takes (gk-final3).
roi-mishpati.listen: The second model (ivrit large-v3) hears the bare name as «רואים משפטי» at every pace (0/26 takes: gk-ab-fw, gk-ab-speed) while the primary hears רועי משפתי on every take; one listen should confirm ro-I mish-pa-TI is clean (mish-PA-ti, ʁoʔˈi miʃpˈati, is the alternative stress). The second model (ivrit large-v3) hears the name clip as «רואים משפטי» (0/26 takes at three paces); RO-ʔi fixes that model but the primary then hears «רוי». Accepted as is for Adam's ear: check reports it as a note.
